paragraphs: The core of the work of agricultural equipment operators (agricultural equipment operation direction) is turning an agronomic plan into safe, accurate, recordable mechanised operations: set the implement parameters to the prescription and the field conditions, work along the route, watch the equipment and crop condition, stop the machine first when something is wrong and then escalate, and leave an operation record. When judging fit, first look at whether you can keep up attention through open-air farming seasons, long hours of driving and strict stop-work rules, and only then consider interests.

Editorial exercise: using the fictional Maiwan MW-V1 task statement below, calculate the covered, missed and double-covered area of six work strips, and write up the 'missing guard' anomaly and the handover record. Everything is done on paper, with no contact with real machinery, pesticides or control systems; observe whether you are willing to recheck the intervals and keep the anomaly and revision records.

Editorial observation suggestion: pay attention to how you react to repeated rechecking, open-air and working-hour conditions, anomaly recording and asking about boundaries. The paper exercise does not test actual driving ability and does not predict hiring, long-term performance or accident probability; actual conditions must be checked with the target employer.

Insufficient evidence: no precise Chinese wage sample for this occupation was obtained. The U.S. wage is the OEWS 45-2091 employee wage (2025, month 5 (May)); employment uses the BLS 2025—2035 projection for this occupation: 66,900 → 72,600 people, with the OOH rounded growth at 9%, table 1.2 at 8.6%, and about 10,100 openings per year. The NBS2025 broad-category average does not replace this occupation's wage; the wage survey scope is not the same as the employment projection scope.

In one sentence: a mechanised role that puts an agronomic prescription into the field, relying on equipment checks, working to the rules and stopping on an anomaly, not on driving the machine as fast as possible; safety and records are part of the job.

The tasks of agricultural equipment operators fall into three categories: preparation and execution (pre-shift checks, hitching implements, setting parameters, cultivating, harvesting or crop protection along the route); equipment and site tending (watching and listening to the equipment, clearing blockages, doing light maintenance and reporting faults); and recording and collaboration (weighing records, saving operation data, communicating anomalies to supervisors and agronomists). The weight of the three varies with the tillage, harvest and transport, and crop protection directions.

O*NET 45-2091.00 agricultural equipment operators: drive and control equipment to support agricultural activities such as tilling soil, planting, cultivating and harvesting crops, feeding and herding livestock, or cleaning animal waste; they may also bale crops or stack hay, and run post-harvest stationary equipment such as shelling, threshing and cotton ginning. Core tasks include loading and unloading crops, mixing and loading seed or chemicals to the prescription, watching and listening for equipment faults, operating controls to adjust mechanisms, operating tractors, combine harvesters and irrigation equipment, and adjusting and repairing farm machinery and notifying a supervisor of faults. This profile is a U.S. single-occupation basis.

entries: Work preparation｜Inspection and hitching｜Walk around the machine to check oil, water and safety devices, hitch the plough, harrow, seeder or sprayer as the job requires, and confirm the connection is secure.

Field work｜Tillage, sowing and harvesting｜Operate the tractor, seeder and combine harvester along the route and to the parameters, keeping the line straight and the headland turns good, and avoiding missed and double work.

Crop protection work｜Mixing and spraying｜Mix and load fertiliser or pesticide to the label and the prescription, work to the wind speed, temperature and no-entry requirements, and handle protection and decontamination properly.

Equipment tending｜Observation and light maintenance｜Watch and listen to how the equipment is running, clear blockages, do light maintenance such as lubrication and filters, and stop and report on an anomaly.
Transport and records｜Weighing and transport｜Drive a truck to transport crops, supplies or people, and weigh and record the crop quantity and operation data.
Precision work｜Navigation and variable application｜Read prescription maps and navigation data, calibrate sensors, check coverage and save the operation records.

Safety and protection｜27% wear ordinary protective equipment every day, 31% are exposed to contaminants every day, and 39% have a very high level of responsibility for the health and safety of others.
Equipment and attention｜The editors suggest checking people's positions, headlands and blind spots; this page did not quantify fatigue or accident rates.
Editorial check suggestion｜For a real job, check separately the people's positions, equipment guards, stop-work procedures and handover contacts, and do not extrapolate these U.S. shares to China.
Pre-shift checks and hitching are the precondition for safe work and cannot be skipped.

The BLS agricultural workers page contains a combined group and occupation sub-rows. The combined group has 831,900 people in 2025 and 818,700 in 2035, growth of -2% and a net change of -13,300 people (each rounded separately in the table), with about 111,500 openings per year. The equipment operators sub-row 45-2091 goes from 66,900 → 72,600 people, growth of 9% and a net increase of 5,700 people; the median wage in 2025, month 5 (May), is 41,730 U.S. dollars. Pre-shift check: walk around the machine to check oil, water, tyres, lights, guards and safety devices, and confirm the fire extinguisher and first-aid supplies are in place. → Hitching and setting: hitch the implement for the job, check the drawbar and hydraulic connections, and set parameters such as seeding rate or spray rate to the prescription. → Trial work: check coverage, depth and blockages in a short trial run, and only enter the field once it is confirmed normal. → Field work: work along the route and at the set speed, watch the equipment and crop condition, and confirm people's positions first at headlands and blind spots. → Anomaly handling: on hearing an abnormal noise, or on a blockage, missed spray or a person entering the work area, stop the machine first and then call for repair or escalate. → Records and handover: record the worked area, parameters, anomalies and fuel, and hand over the equipment condition at the end of the shift.

Before work: check the weather, wind speed, soil moisture and any no-entry requirements, and confirm whether work is possible. → Coverage check: use navigation or markers to check the working width and any misses or overlaps, and adjust parameters if needed. → Consumable records: record the quantity and batch of seed, fertiliser or chemical. → Equipment status: record faults, repairs and reasons for stopping. → Data saving: save the operation maps and parameters for later checking. → Handover communication: pass anomalies and unfinished items to the next shift or the supervisor.

Work Safety Law of the People's Republic of China (amended in 2021, Presidential Order No. 88): production and business units must establish an all-staff work safety responsibility system and provide work safety education and training to their workers; workers must comply with work safety rules and operating procedures and use labour protection equipment correctly. Specific requirements for pesticide use and farm machinery operation follow the label, industry procedures and local regulations.

Output is measured by whether the work was completed to the prescription, whether the coverage can be checked and whether anomalies were recorded, not by the working speed.

Driving a tractor or combine harvester in mainland China requires the driving licence for the corresponding permitted machine type under Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs rules; in-house training is not a substitute. Road transport qualifications are checked separately by vehicle and use. Pesticide use must comply with the label scope, method, dose and protection requirements, and a supervisor's approval cannot waive a label restriction or allow equipment guards to be bypassed.
Anomalies and the reasons for stopping should be recorded truthfully and not hidden because they affect progress.
The conclusion of one operation applies only to that field, machine, parameter set and weather condition; one successful operation must not be extrapolated to all fields or all machines.

Before starting the job, check at least six things: whether the position is in tillage, sowing, harvest and transport, crop protection or precision work; the equipment type and whether road driving is included; whether pesticide handling and the corresponding protection are involved; the working hours and peak-season arrangements; the training and licence requirements; and the anomaly stop and reporting rules.

Type of work and equipment: tillage and sowing, harvest and transport, crop protection spraying, or precision work? Whether driving on public roads is required.

Check the target employer's education and training requirements. The BLS agricultural workers combined group usually has no formal education threshold and provides on-the-job training; equipment operators may need fuller training or relevant experience, and no uniform Chinese threshold or fixed number of training days can be inferred.

For employment conditions in China, check the labour contract; protection and training obligations are also covered by the Work Safety Law, and pesticide use requirements by the Pesticide Administration Regulations, and employer rules alone cannot replace them.
Safety and protection: protective equipment, pesticide handling and decontamination procedures, heat and dust protection, and the inspection requirements for machinery guards.

For farm machinery driving in China, check the driving licence by permitted machine type; for the safe use of pesticides, check the protection, labelling and applicable-entity record requirements under Articles 33—36 of the regulations.

Chinese tractor and combine harvester driving licences are limited to permitted machine types; road transport conditions are checked separately, and using pesticides does not amount to holding a production or business licence. The U.S. BLS also notes that some equipment positions require a driving licence and that pesticide handling may require a state applicator licence, which must not be applied to China.
For cross-region work, check the licences and any restricted-work requirements under the destination's regulations.
Anomaly and reporting rules: which situations require stopping the machine, whom to report to, and whether simple faults may be cleared independently.

values: Maiwan MW-V1 fictional task statement

Maiwan MW-V1｜Original paper task statement: a rectangle of 100m × 24m, area 2,400m²; work runs along the 100m direction with a nominal working width of 4m. It practises geometric coverage and recording only and contains no real machine type, speed, pesticide dose or operating parameter. Six planned strips: W1[0,4], W2[4,8], W3[8,12], W4[12,16], W5[16,20], W6[20,24]; the square brackets are the lateral metre intervals, the boundary-line area is 0, and each strip is 100m long.

Fictional actual log: W1[0,4], W2[4,8], W3[8,12], W4[12,16], W5[17,21], W6[20,24]. Status card: W5 has a missing guard, cause and recovery unconfirmed; all logs are only a task statement and cannot be treated as a real equipment operation record.

On day 5 change only the W5 strip to [16,20] and leave the other strips unchanged; the missing-guard status is retained. Recalculate coverage and explain why a met area still cannot produce an equipment clearance conclusion.
Exercise tasks and deliverables

Task one: draw the six strips and calculate the area of each strip, the total area, the union of the strips, the omission and the overlap, and write out the coverage ratio with the working. Task two: write up the missing-guard status, the unknown recovery information, the parties awaiting confirmation and the handover items; write only a paper anomaly record and do not design real equipment stop-control steps.
Task three: recalculate with the day 5 input and give a 'geometric coverage conclusion' and an 'equipment status conclusion' separately; the former must not cancel the latter.
Reference answers for both versions

Reference answer: each strip is 100×4=400m², giving a total of 2,400m²; the union [0,16]∪[17,24] is 23m wide, uniquely covered 2,300m², so the coverage ratio is 2,300÷2,400≈95.83%. The omission [16,17] is 100m² and the overlap [20,21] is 100m². A total area exactly equal to the plot area does not mean there is no omission, and an overlap cannot cancel an omission; the W5 missing guard is still not confirmed recovered, so no real work clearance conclusion can be given.

Day 5 reference answer: after changing W5 to [16,20] the union is [0,24], uniquely covered 2,400m², 100%, with an omission of 0 and an overlap of 0; the missing guard is still unresolved and clearance still cannot be given. A corrected area does not prove the machinery is safe or actually repaired.
Boundary of the paper-only exercise

Everything is original paper material, and the work does not constitute a real work plan, proof of driving ability or an equipment clearance record; it involves no machinery, chemicals or real control system. Real work additionally requires lawful qualifications, training, the equipment manual and field confirmation; an unconfirmed guard problem must not be ignored because of progress, an AI answer or a met coverage figure.

values: Requirements and status matrix

Requirements matrix｜Record 100×24m, the six strips with their planned and actual intervals, and the missing-guard status; mark the input, working and unknown items for each. Map the coverage requirement to the union of the strips and the safety status to the anomaly record; keep the two conditions separate and do not merge them into one pass mark.
Keep the original input and the day 5 revision as separate versions, and do not write the strip correction up as a guard repair.
Independent area recheck

Independent recheck｜Without looking at the original working, recalculate the uniquely covered area of 2,300m², the omission of 100m² and the overlap of 100m² from the strip map. Check why 400m²×6=2,400m² cannot prove full coverage; mark [16,17] and [20,21] on the map.
The day 5 recheck shows the uniquely covered area of 2,400m² coexisting with the missing guard, confirming that the geometric conclusion does not cover the safety status.
One-page summary and handover

One-page summary｜Submit the strip maps for both versions, the area working, the coverage ratio, the anomalies and the items awaiting confirmation. Handover note｜State the MW-V1 fictional task statement, the unresolved W5 guard status and that only the paper recheck was completed, with no real operation or clearance.
Tools and the author's role

Tools note｜Pen and paper or a spreadsheet may be used, with the formulas and the human recheck listed; AI may assist with organisation only and the results still have to be checked. Role statement｜The author completed the fictional log calculations; there is no driving, field servicing or equipment approval experience, and the paper work is not written up as hands-on experience.

rows: Editorial example｜Safety knowledge screening
Whether the person can state the pre-shift check items, the purpose of the guards and the stop conditions.
Able to explain each checklist item in turn and point out which situations require stopping the machine.
Treating safety devices as optional, or being unable to state the stop conditions, is a clear risk signal.
Editorial example｜Practical observation
Whether the sequence for the walk-around check, hitching and starting is correct.
Operates to procedure and proactively confirms blind spots and people's positions.
Real observation requires lawful qualifications, machine-type training and a controlled environment; the exercise on this page is paper only and does not amount to passing a practical assessment.
Editorial example｜Work quality assessment
Whether the parameter setting and coverage check meet the prescription requirements.
The operation record and coverage data can be checked and the anomalies are explained.
Work that reports only a completed area, without coverage or anomaly records, cannot be judged for quality.
Editorial example｜Trial period
Whether checks are done to process, anomalies are reported promptly and records are kept complete.
Able to complete a single-machinery operation independently and pass review.
One performance or one reminder cannot be used to infer long-term fit directly; judge after checking the training, the tasks and the feedback.

items.title: What may be assessed in interviews and the trial period, and which conclusions cannot be inferred?

values: Day 1｜Organise the fictional inputs
Transcribe the MW-V1 plot, the six planned strips, the six actual strips and the guard status; submit the input sheet and confirm it is paper-only throughout.
Day 2｜Draw the strips
Draw the W1—W6 lateral strips and mark the omission [16,17] and the overlap [20,21]; submit a checkable sketch.
Day 3｜Calculate coverage
Calculate 400m² per strip, a total of 2,400m², a union of 2,300m² and 95.83% coverage; give the units and the working.
Day 4｜Anomaly handover
Write up the W5 missing guard, the unknown recovery and the items awaiting confirmation; submit a paper handover record and generate no real operating instruction.
Day 5｜Change one input
Change only W5 to [16,20] and recalculate the coverage of 2,400m², the omission of 0 and the overlap of 0; the missing guard is retained and clearance cannot be given.
Day 6｜Independent recheck
Cover the original answers and recalculate both versions from the strips, checking that coverage and safety status stay separate; keep the error-correction record.
Day 7｜Observation and next steps
Submit a one-page summary recording how checking and revising felt and the machine types and jurisdictional conditions still to be learnt; one exercise does not predict fit or hiring.

items.title: Seven-day experience: complete one full agricultural equipment operator task cycle using fictional material

entries: Observe the changes: are the strip map, the working and the answers consistent, and which item went wrong at some point?
Task choice: do you prefer rechecking routes, anomalies or records? This is an editorial observation and does not represent a real division of work.
Exercise cost: record the time taken and how repeated rechecking felt; do not infer real driving tolerance.
Material boundary: can you distinguish a met paper coverage figure from an unresolved missing guard?
Reaction to feedback: after finding an omission, do you keep the original input and explain the revision?
Interest in the process: are you willing to explain the formulas, the unknowns and the reason clearance cannot be given?
Next steps: check the target machine type, the driving licence, the employer's training and the tasks; completing the paper work does not lead straight into real independent work.
